topic.title: Check Out a Branch
topic.shortdesc: Use the Checkout action in the Git History view to switch to an existing local branch, create a new branch, or check out a commit in detached HEAD state.

body.p: Use the Checkout action in the Git History view to check out a commit. The Checkout dialog offers three modes:

ul.li: Switch to existing local branch — checks out a local branch that points to the selected commit.
Create a new branch — creates a new branch from the selected commit and checks it out.
Detached HEAD — checks out the commit without creating or switching to any branch.

body.p:
To open the Checkout dialog, follow these steps:
On Git History, select a commit and right-click it to open the context menu.
Choose Checkout and the Checkout dialog opens.

fig.title: Git History Checkout from Context Menu

section.title: Switch to an Existing Local Branch
section.p: If only one local branch points to the selected commit, double-click the commit row to switch to the branch.
The Double-click to switch to this branch hint shows in the tooltip that appears when you hover over a commit that is associated with a local branch.

fig.title: Double-click to switch to this branch hint

ol.li: On Checkout, select Switch to existing local branch.
(Optional) If multiple local branches track the selected commit, choose which branch you to check out from the dropdown.
Select Checkout to switch to another existing local branch.

section.title: Create a new branch
section.p: To create a new branch, follow these steps:

ol.li:
On Checkout, choose Create a new branch.
(Optional) If the selected commit is associated with a remote branch, enter a unique branch name on Branch name or choose which of its associated remote branches to track on Track remote branch.
If the selected commit only associated with a local repository, enter a unique branch name on Branch name.
Select Checkout to check out and switch to a new local branch from the remote branch.

section.p: The new branch is configured automatically and does not need further setup.

section.title: Create a Detached HEAD
section.p: To only view or make experimental changes to a branch, check out the commit as a detached HEAD.
To do so, from the Checkout dialog, choose Detached HEAD and select Checkout.

p.note: Changes made on a detached HEAD are temporary. To keep your changes, move them to an existing branch or create a new one.

section.p: An amber HEAD label displays next to the commit while in detached HEAD form.

fig.title: Git History, HEAD label
fig.note: If you have uncommitted changes on your current branch, the Switch branch dialog appears and prompts you to stash or move changes, or cancel the switch to another branch.
